title: Your face and mine look beautiful
odia:
ବଗ ମୁହଁ ଚାହିଁ ବଗୁଲୀ ବସେ
ତୋ ମୁହଁ ମୋ ମୁହଁ ସୁନ୍ଦର ଦିଶେ।
literal_meaning: The female egret sits looking at the egret’s face; your face and my face look beautiful.
meaning_odia: ବଗର ମୁହଁକୁ ଚାହିଁ ବଗୁଲୀ ବସିଛି; ପର ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ତୋ ମୁହଁ ଓ ମୋ ମୁହଁ ଦୁହେଁ ସୁନ୍ଦର ଦିଶୁଥିବା କଥା ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ପରସ୍ପର ପ୍ରଶଂସା ସହ ନିଜକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ସେହି ପ୍ରଶଂସାରେ ସାମିଲ କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର। କହିବାର ସ୍ୱର ଅନୁସାରେ ସ୍ନେହ ବା ଥଟ୍ଟା ଥାଇପାରେ; କାହାକୁ ଅସୁନ୍ଦର ବା କପଟୀ ବୋଲି ପଙ୍କ୍ତିଟି କହୁନାହିଁ।
explanation: The gaze at another face leads to a favourable judgement that includes both “you” and “me.” Our editorial reading is of mutual admiration that also makes room for self-admiration. The scene can be affectionate or teasing; the wording alone does not turn it into an accusation of dishonest praise.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Two friends each admire the other’s portrait and then praise their own. Someone fondly quotes the egret pair and its verdict on “your face and mine.”
cultural_context: The bird pair gives the judgement a small scene rather than an abstract lesson. Repeating ମୁହଁ and moving from ବଗ to ତୋ and ମୋ lets the image pass from birds to a speaking pair without specifying a human relationship.

english_summary: A paired gaze leads to admiration that includes both the other and oneself.
